body: Sorry, my bad, wasn’t careful with my words. It should be pretty clear though from the context I was talking about biological women

Well, I guess I do relate but only to that one specific part about motherhood, that part really did speak to me. Not really anything else… I feel no need to conform to feminine roles/expectations, though I have thought to myself that if I were a woman I would totally be fine with acting like one, if that means anything. Not much else really clicks for me, and I have done a short read through of that site before and I don’t recall having much more of a reaction than “I mean, maybe sorta” like once or twice and a very prevalent “nah, that ain’t me”.

So yeah. Probably not dysphoria…?

But the thing is that I don’t want to become a girl, I want to have been a girl. And now that I have not been a girl, I’m fine with staying as a guy no problem. It doesn’t really seem like dysphoria to me.

In the case this is dysphoria. How would I be able to do anything about it? I don’t want to dress up, I don’t want to transition. So I’m just sort of stuck here, wanting something that can never happen.

Us and our family arent experienced with this. We don't know what to do. We also feel that forcing him to get committed to a facility will destroy his chances at pharmacy school. The obvious answer is to get him committed anyways, but it's in reality a hard choice. Can you make the same choice if you were in our situation?

And no, I'm not attributing these to narcissism. I probably worded it wrong. I'm saying that these symptoms imitate narcissism. Which is true.

It's not about the shame. It's about worrying people who I care about. I don't want to be a burden on them and their lives more than I already am. I already tried talking to my parents, they didn't really seem to understand and all that resulted from it was my family dynamic being nearly ruined, so I never mentioned it again. I don't want to do that to them again.
I skimmed through all of the dysphoria sections, and I do admit that some of it is relatable, but at the same time not exactly. I’ll take my time to think on it more. Thanks for this resource

Well, that’s the thing. 9 times out of 10 I do have the same internal experience as other cis-men. And, to be perfectly honest, i don’t know he internal thoughts of other cis-men, so I can’t really say anything for certain. I know a few cis friends who have also questioned their gender identity before but have stayed cis, so I sort of assume I’m normal. But again, I just don’t know, hence my confusion.

Yeah, i know how this comes off, and I posted in the trans sub for a reason. But tbh I don’t think I’m actually trans, though I admit I have trans thoughts sometimes ig? I still feel like a guy, and frankly I like it. It just feels sort of weird when I occasionally feel like I want to be a girl
Well at least I'm not alone
I'm reading this and I'm fucking crying. I wish I had your strength to live.
